As Johnson & Johnson (JNJ) Shares Declined, First Manhattan Company Has Raised Its Position; Schlumberger LTD (SLB) Holder Matrix Asset Advisors Cut Stake by $363,648
June 7, 2018 - By wolcottdaily
First Manhattan Company increased its stake in Johnson & Johnson (JNJ) by 1.16% based on its latest 2018Q1 regulatory filing with the SEC. First Manhattan Company bought 27,526 shares as the company’s stock declined 8.03% with the market. The hedge fund held 2.40 million shares of the major pharmaceuticals company at the end of 2018Q1, valued at $308.04 million, up from 2.38 million at the end of the previous reported quarter. First Manhattan Company who had been investing in Johnson & Johnson for a number of months, seems to be bullish on the $329.34 billion market cap company. The stock increased 1.08% or $1.31 during the last trading session, reaching $122.79. About 6.80M shares traded or 1.21% up from the average. Johnson & Johnson (NYSE:JNJ) has declined 4.75% since June 7, 2017 and is downtrending. It has underperformed by 17.32% the S&P500. The institutional investor held 185,140 shares of the oilfield services and equipment company at the end of 2018Q1, valued at $11.99M, down from 190,822 at the end of the previous reported quarter. Matrix Asset Advisors Inc who had been investing in Schlumberger Ltd for a number of months, seems to be less bullish one the $95.42B market cap company.
